item.title: 310577 : I-71/75 North-South between MM 188.5 and 191.7 Between Kyles Lane and Brent Spence Bridge in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : UPDATE (Nov. 5, 2026) -- The traffic impacts for Wednesday, Nov. 5 as part of the ongoing electrical project for the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project have been adjusted. Work tonight (Thursday, Nov. 5), will include a double left lane closure on Interstates 71/75 northbound in the project area. A single left lane closure will take place at 8 p.m. This will shift to a double left lane closure beginning at 11 p.m. A single right lane closure on I-71/75 southbound will be in place beginning at 8 p.m. All lanes reopen by 5 a.m. on Friday, Nov. 6. Work is expected to continue with single left lane closure in both directions overnight as the project progresses. KYTC will provide updates if additional traffic impacts are required to complete the project. This electrical work is expected to be completed by Monday, Nov. 30. COVINGTON, Ky. (Sept. 25, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of nightly lane closures on Interstates 71/75 in Kenton County beginning Monday, Sept. 28. Crews will be performing electrical work as part of the ongoing Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project. This work will require a nightly northbound and southbound left lane closure from Kyles Lane (KY 1072) (188.52 mile point) to the Brent Spence Bridge (191.63 mile point), a distance of 3.11 miles. Both left lanes (northbound and southbound) will be blocked from 8 p.m. to 5 a.m. All lanes will reopen by 5 a.m. No lane closures associated with this portion of the project will be in place from Thursday, Oct. 8 through Sunday, Oct. 11 due to BLINK. Weather permitting, this portion of the project is expected to be completed Friday, Oct. 23. Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances. About the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project The Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project is one of the nation’s most significant transportation transformations, spanning eight miles of I-71/75 in Kentucky and I-75 in Ohio. Construction will begin with the new companion bridge to the west of the Brent Spence Bridge and one mile of approach work in each state. In addition to the new bridge, the project will restripe the existing Brent Spence Bridge to carry local traffic; improve safety and reduce congestion by separating local and through travel; redesign ramp configurations throughout the corridor; and add new pedestrian and bicycle connections linking neighborhoods to jobs and transit. This once-in-a-generation investment will strengthen national freight movement, support local businesses and workforce growth, and enhance quality of life for the millions who rely on this critical corridor. The project team coordinates with all navigation apps so drivers can easily determine the best route from their starting point to their destination. For more information, visit brentspencebridgecorridor.com.

item.title: 292981 : I-71/75 South Ramp from 12th Street/MLK Jr. Boulevard in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : Interstate 71/75 ramp closures and detours in Covington are needed to safely advance construction on the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project, which will add interstate lanes, better access, a new companion bridge and convert the existing bridge for local travel to improve safety and increase regional highway capacity. Temporary closures and detours will take place in multiple phases. On or after Wednesday, Dec. 23, crews will reopen Bullock Avenue from Pike Street (U.S. 25) to 12th Street (KY 1120). Additionally, the Interstates 71/75 on-ramp from Bullock Avenue will reopen. Bullock Avenue has been widened and extended west of the interstate to accommodate room for additional interstate lanes that will be put in place as part of the project. Significant utility work occurred in this area during the closure that was necessary to be performed prior to the reopening of the road and ramp. The ramp from Bullock Avenue to I-71/75 southbound is considered to be in its final configuration and no major work in the future is anticipated as part of this project. KYTC will provide further updates via the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project website. [https://brentspencebridgecorridor.com/] Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances.

item.title: 254857 : I-264 East-West between MM 21.5 and 22.9 Area of US-42 in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : To minimize extended traffic impacts in the area, the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) and I-264 and U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) Widening and Improvement Project team have combined project construction phasing into a single approach. The schedule for upcoming temporary traffic impacts listed below takes into consideration the potential for inclement weather and the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday. Beginning Friday, Nov. 20, at 8 p.m. through Monday, Nov. 23, at 6 a.m. The I-264 East on-ramp from U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) will be closed. The I-264 West off-ramp to U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) at Exit 22 will be closed. Beginning Monday, Nov. 23, at 6 a.m., through Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 6 a.m. The I-264 West on-ramp from U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) will be closed. Beginning Monday, Nov. 23, at 6 a.m. through Wednesday, Nov. 25, at 6 a.m. The I-264 East off-ramp to U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) at Exit 22 will be closed. Motorists will still be able to access KY 22 at Exit 22 and should detour by turning left onto Lime Kiln Lane to reconnect with either eastbound or westbound U.S. 42. By 6 a.m. on Monday, Nov. 23, traffic will be shifted onto the newly constructed portion of the U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) bridge over I-264. All temporary traffic restrictions associated with the traffic shift are expected to be lifted by 6 a.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 25. This traffic configuration will remain in place through the Summer of 2027 as crews advance construction on the remaining portion of the bridge. The upcoming traffic shift marks a significant project milestone, with construction on the $130 million project now more than halfway complete. ​ U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) eastbound is reduced to one through lane west of Rudy Lane, and U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) westbound is reduced to one through lane at Northfield Drive. ***Turning movements from U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) to I-264 East and West on-ramps are not affected. These traffic control measures are expected to remain in place throughout the reconstruction of the U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) bridge over I-264 (Watterson Expressway). Traffic is currently shifted to the outside shoulders on I-264 East and West (Watterson Expressway) between KY 1447 (Westport Road) and I-71

item.title: 269220 : I-71 North-South between MM 0.1 and 2.0 Between I-64/I-71 Interchange and Zorn Ave. in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The I-71 widening and improvement project is a $50 million infrastructure investment to enhance safety and improve mobility along one of Louisville's most critical travel corridors. The two-year project, focused on increasing traffic capacity and safety, will enhance regional connectivity, provide reliable travel for years to come, and support economic growth. The project spans approximately two miles of interstate from the I-65/I-71 interchange near Frankfort Avenue to the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange. Additional improvements include the construction of a multi-use path along Zorn Avenue between the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange and Mellwood Avenue, as well as a new median treatment at the intersection of Zorn Avenue and Mellwood Avenue to enhance safety and better define traffic movements. The project also includes the demolition and reconstruction of the I-71 bridge over Beargrass Creek, along with a latex overlay on the I-71 bridge over I-64 at mile point 0.3 to extend the structure’s service life. For additional information, please visit https://transportation.ky.gov/DistrictFive/Pages/I-71-Widening---Louisville-.aspx.

item.title: 292980 : I-71/75 North Ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Boulevard in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : Interstate 71/75 ramp closures and detours in Covington are needed to safely advance construction on the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project, which will add interstate lanes, better access, a new companion bridge and convert the existing bridge for local travel to improve safety and increase regional highway capacity. Temporary closures and detours will now begin on Monday, June 8, and will take place in multiple phases. I-71/75 northbound off-ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Blvd. (0.0 - 0.28 mile points): this closure will remain in place through Summer 2027. Detour: Traffic will use the I-71/75 northbound 5th Street exit ramp, turn left (north) onto Philadelphia Street, then left onto 4th Street driving west to the I-71/75 southbound ramp to Pike Street. Turn left on to Pike Street, then right on to Simon Kenton Way, then left on to MLK Blvd. KYTC will provide further updates ahead of the closures to inform all road users via the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project website. [https://brentspencebridgecorridor.com/] Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances.
